clue.text: Come unstuck about team in country

indicators.note: the rearranged letters wrap around the team, holding it in their middle
to come unstuck is to fall apart, so the letters of the word come are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: XI is eleven in Roman numerals, the size of a football or cricket side

explanation.surface: A side falls apart while touring abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Come unstuck' reads like the surface verb phrase, but 'unstuck' is the anagram signal working on 'Come' alone, giving MECO.
explanation.definitionFit: Mexico is a nation of Central America, an example of the general word.

clue.text: Ostentatious sign of affection — there's nothing 'live' about it!

definitions.text: Ostentatious sign of affection — there's nothing 'live' about it!

parts.words: Ostentatious sign of affection — there's nothing 'live' about it!
parts.note: the joke is that no living creature delivered a real attack, and swapping the vowel of live for nothing (O) gives the first word

explanation.surface: A conspicuous token of fondness, with the playful claim that nothing about it is alive.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation mark flags the play: change the I of 'live' to O (nothing) and you have the first word. It also starts the theme song title Somebody to Love.
explanation.definitionFit: A hickey or bruise from kissing is a very visible, rather showy token of passion.

clue.text: Derisive statement about subsequent pages — issue for president

indicators.note: the derisive remark is wrapped around the page reference, which sits in its middle

parts.note: a jeer is a mocking remark
ff. is the abbreviation for 'and the following pages'
issue means offspring, so a son

explanation.surface: A sneering remark about later pages becomes a matter for the head of state.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Jefferson was the third US President; his name also opens the band name Jefferson Airplane.

clue.text: Tips for watering houseplants if they're etiolated and pale

indicators.note: the tips of words are their front ends, so take the opening letter of each of the five words that follow

explanation.surface: Gardening advice: water your houseplants if they have gone pale and spindly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Etiolated' is a botanist's word for plants blanched by lack of light; it sits nicely with 'pale'.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: something drained of colour is described with this word.

clue.text: Formal study of poet

parts.note: dry can mean stiff, impersonal and formal in manner
a den is a private room for working, a study

explanation.surface: An academic study of a poet, done formally.
explanation.definitionFit: John Dryden was the leading English poet of the Restoration and the first Poet Laureate.

clue.text: It's being unspecified what 3 24 sang to 2

definitions.meaning: a person whose identity is not stated, as in 'someone called'
3 and 24 together name the band Jefferson Airplane, whose 1967 hit was titled with this word followed by 'to' and the 2-down's first word

explanation.surface: A puzzle-referencing riddle about an unnamed being and a song.
explanation.walkthrough: Cross-references: 3 + 24 make JEFFERSON AIRPLANE, and 2 is LOVE, giving the song Somebody to Love.
explanation.definitionFit: A pronoun for an unnamed person, and the opening word of the famous psychedelic rock song.

clue.text: You once flipped, getting into cannabis, ecstasy and mescal

indicators.note: the turned-round pronoun goes inside the word for cannabis

parts.note: pot is slang for cannabis

indicators.note: flipped over, so the old pronoun is read backwards

parts.note: ye is the archaic form of you
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Someone flipped out after getting into drugs: cannabis, ecstasy and mescal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'You once' is the old pronoun, a common crossword convention for archaic forms; 'flipped' sounds like losing one's mind but signals the turnaround.
explanation.definitionFit: Mescal buttons are the dried tops of the hallucinogenic cactus, so the two names are interchangeable.

clue.text: Agreement on extension in house near Big Apple

indicators.note: near means placed next to, so the city follows
the extension sits inside the abbreviation for house

parts.note: an arm is an extension sticking out from a body or building
the Big Apple is a nickname for New York, NY

explanation.surface: Neighbours agree on a house extension near New York.
explanation.definitionFit: Harmony is accord between people, a synonym of agreement.

clue.text: Maybe Trump lifts their hearts, protecting America from Islam

definitions.note: the singer Cat Stevens took the name Yusuf Islam; this is the name that precedes his surname

indicators.note: the central letters wrap around America, sheltering it
the centre letter of each of the three words before

parts.note: US is the United States

explanation.surface: Perhaps President Trump cheers people up, protecting the USA from Islam.
explanation.walkthrough: The hearts of maYbe, trUmp and liFts are Y, U, F; US goes inside after Y. 'Trump' is just fodder, not the President.
explanation.definitionFit: Yusuf is the forename the musician formerly called Cat Stevens adopted, followed by the surname given here.

clue.text: Line up a little talk

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a bar is a line, as in a musical bar line
a bit is a little

explanation.surface: An instruction to arrange a brief chat.
explanation.walkthrough: RABBIT is British slang for chatter, from the rhyming slang 'rabbit and pork' for talk.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang to chatter on at length is to go on and on, a verb from rhyming slang.

clue.text: Cooper's band

definitions.meaning: the shock rocker ... Cooper's name, and that of his original group, starts with this word
an ... band is a hair band worn across the head, named after the Tenniel drawings

explanation.surface: A rock group belonging to someone named Cooper.
explanation.walkthrough: It also ties to the theme: Jefferson Airplane's White Rabbit retells Alice in Wonderland.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name doubling as Cooper's forename and the headband style named for Lewis Carroll's heroine.

clue.text: Corruption reflected in extremely fierce and violent dissent

indicators.note: taking only the extremes of the word fierce, its first and last letters
violent suggests a wild upheaval, so the letters of dissent are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A political rot shown up in fierce, violent opposition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflected in' is just a link here, not a reversal signal; the anagram of 'dissent' gives TIDNESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Rottenness and a putrid stink are what decay brings, so it fits the rotting sense of the clue word.

clue.text: They publish online, giving scroungers nothing for article

indicators.note: one letter is put in place of another: nothing replaces the article

parts.note: blaggers are people who cadge or wangle things for free
a is the indefinite article
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Web writers who give freeloaders nothing for an article they wrote.
explanation.definitionFit: People who write web logs are, by definition, online publishers.

clue.text: Finally starting to understand ultimate reality?

indicators.note: the final letters of each of the three words after it

explanation.surface: At last a person begins to grasp the ultimate truth.
explanation.definitionFit: In theology the deity is the ultimate ground of being and reality; the question mark admits it is a definition by description.

clue.text: Having energy in volatile type of relationship — it won't happen again

indicators.note: energy is placed in the middle of the relationship word

parts.note: an on-off relationship keeps breaking up and restarting
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A stormy romance that will not be repeated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having' is a link: the relationship has E inside it, ON-E-OFF.
explanation.definitionFit: A unique event, the only one of its kind, is never repeated.

clue.text: Did Clyde finally become criminal? Unquestionably

indicators.note: criminal suggests something crooked, so the letters are bent into a new order
the final letter of the word become

explanation.surface: Did Clyde, of Bonnie and Clyde, end up a criminal? Without doubt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' rearranges DID, CLYDE and E. Clyde Barrow was the famous 1930s American robber.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean beyond doubt, certainly; a synonym.

clue.text: I can be found blocking missile returning 21

definitions.note: the answer to 21 means three, a trio

indicators.note: the letter I sits inside the reversed weapon, blocking its path
the missile comes back, read backwards

parts.note: a dart is a small thrown missile

explanation.surface: I am found obstructing a returning missile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns DART into TRAD; I goes in. 21 is TREBLE, meaning three.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of three is a trio or threesome, which is what a treble also is.

clue.text: It's about being a male amongst others, inherently belonging

indicators.note: the word it wraps around everything else

parts.note: the word it, with the 's acting as 'has' joining it to the rest

indicators.note: the male is placed among the other people

parts.note: men as other people
a man is a male

explanation.surface: Philosophical musing on being one man among others, and belonging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being' is a link word, though it looks philosophical; 'others' stands for other people, men, a loose but fair equivalence.
explanation.definitionFit: Philosophers call a quality present within something, part of its nature, by this word: intrinsic, inherent.

clue.text: I must retract refusal before end of debate

indicators.note: the reversed refusal comes ahead of the last letter
retract means draw back, so the refusal is read backwards

parts.note: no is a refusal

indicators.note: the final letter of the word debate

explanation.surface: Someone must withdraw their refusal before a debate ends.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman numeral I is the number one.

clue.text: For example, you're probably thinking initially of this country

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so take the first letter of each of the three following words

explanation.surface: A guessing-game claim: you are probably picturing this land.
explanation.definitionFit: Egypt is the African nation of the pyramids, the land the clue invites you to picture.

clue.text: Not extremely upset about thoughtful communication

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the middle letters are read backwards
removing the extremes, the first and last letters of upset

explanation.surface: A not-so-upset person reflects on a considerate message.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not extremely' leaves PSE from UPSET; 'about' turns it to E S P.
explanation.definitionFit: Extrasensory perception, telepathy, is communication by thought alone; the wit is in the literal 'thoughtful'.

clue.text: Three get high, as we hear

definitions.meaning: ... as a number means threefold, triple
a high-pitched sound, such as a boy soprano voice or the top end of an audio setting

explanation.surface: Three people get high, so we are told.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as we hear' looks like a sound-alike signal but simply says the highness is of sound, pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripled or threefold, and also the high register in music or sound reproduction.

clue.text: Uncle came back carrying a bit of melon in season

indicators.note: the reversed uncle holds the bit of melon inside
came back means the name is read backwards

parts.note: Uncle Remus is the storyteller of Joel Chandler Harris's tales

indicators.note: just the first letter of the word melon

explanation.surface: An uncle returned with some melon in season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'came back' turns REMUS into SUMER; M goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The warmest of the four times of the year.

clue.text: Smooth start to surprising defeat

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word surprising

parts.note: to lick an opponent is to beat them

explanation.surface: A smooth opening to an unexpected defeat.
explanation.walkthrough: It also completes the theme: Grace Slick sang with Jefferson Airplane.
explanation.definitionFit: Glossy and slippery, or glib and polished: a synonym.

clue.text: Stare in astonishment at the last replacement

indicators.note: a startled state, so the letters of stare are jolted out of order

parts.note: Z is the last letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone gapes in amazement at a final substitute.
explanation.definitionFit: A word from German for a substitute, typically an inferior imitation.

clue.text: Time spent organising perinatal transport in Texas

indicators.note: organising puts the remaining letters into a new order
spent means used up and gone, so the time is removed

explanation.surface: Arranging time for maternity care in Texas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spent' removes T from PERINATAL; 'organising' rearranges what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: The American term for an aircraft, so an air transport as named in Texas.

clue.text: Schemer pulled switcheroo to learn about source of gold

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the source of gold
a switcheroo is a swap, so the letters of learn are switched around
the source of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A conman's swap trick to find where the gold comes from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pulled switcheroo' rearranges LEARN into ANLER; G goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone angling for something, fishing for advantage, is a schemer.

clue.text: Elegance comes from good breeding

parts.note: race as lineage, stock or breeding

explanation.surface: Elegance is the product of good upbringing.
explanation.walkthrough: Theme: Grace Slick of Jefferson Airplane.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: poise and refinement of movement.

clue.text: No charge for accommodation on island

definitions.text: No charge for accommodation on island

parts.words: No charge for accommodation on island
parts.note: the name of Yeats's lake isle reads as a three-word sentence saying the hostelry costs nothing

explanation.surface: An island where lodging is free.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the name as INN IS FREE. The Lake Isle of Innisfree is in Lough Gill, Ireland, the subject of a W. B. Yeats poem.
explanation.definitionFit: A small island in Lough Gill, County Sligo, famous from Yeats's poem.

clue.text: Starts to brush almond paste on roll

indicators.note: the starting letters of the two words brush and almond

parts.note: gel is a jelly-like paste

explanation.surface: Baking instructions: brush almond paste on to a bread roll.
explanation.definitionFit: A ring-shaped bread roll, boiled then baked.

clue.text: See 2
Check briefly on cattle moving in playground once

definitions.note: relating to motion, and the name of the Kinetic Playground, a Chicago rock venue of the late 1960s

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the cattle come first

parts.note: kine is an old plural of cow

indicators.note: cut short, the check mark loses its last letter

parts.note: a tick is a check mark

explanation.surface: Checking quickly on cattle wandering about an old playground.
explanation.walkthrough: The Kinetic Playground was a Chicago psychedelic rock club where Jefferson Airplane played, hence 'once'.
explanation.definitionFit: Of or caused by motion, and the first word of a vanished Chicago venue's name.

clue.text: Left parent scratching head in a state of agitation

indicators.note: scratching out the head removes the first letter

parts.note: a father is a parent

explanation.surface: A father left alone, head-scratching and anxious.
explanation.definitionFit: To be worked up into a sweat, flustered, is to be 'in a' froth of this kind; an idiom.
